questions.question_text: ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral. BC is extended to meet the tangent at A at E. If BC = 4.5cm, BE = 8cm and $\angle CDA=\angle BAE+\angle BEA$, then find the radius of the circle.
questions.solution_text:
It is given that $\angle CDA=\angle BAE+\angle BEA$ and as per the exterior angle property of triangle - $\angle CBA=\angle BAE+\angle BEA$
=> $\angle CDA=\angle CBA$ and since it is a cyclic quadrilateral,$\angle CDA+\angle CBA=180^{\circ\ }$
=> $\angle CDA=\angle CBA=90^{\circ\ }$
And since $\angle CBA=90^{\circ\ }$, thus AC will be the diameter as diameter subtends at $90^{\circ\ }$. 
Now, as per tangent secant theorem - 
$EA^2=EB\times EC$ => $EA^2=8\times12.5=100$
=> $EA=10\ cm$
And, since AC is the diameter, $\angle CAE=90^{\circ\ }$. So, by using Pythagoras' theorem -
$CA^2+AE^2=CE^2$
=> $CA^2+10^2=12.5^2$ 
=> $CA=7.5\ cm$
=> Radius of the circle is $3.75\ cm$.

It is given that $n,\ a,\ b$ are in increasing GP with a common ratio equal to $m$. => $a=nm\ and\ b=nm^2$
=> $9m+an=3b$
=> $9m+\left(nm\right)n=3\left(nm^2\right)$
=> $m\left(9+n^2\right)=3\left(nm^2\right)$
=> $m=\dfrac{\left(9+n^2\right)}{3n}\rightarrow1$
Also, $bm+2n=5a$
=> $nm^2\left(m\right)+2n=5\left(mn\right)$
=> $n\left(m^3+2\right)=n\left(5m\right)$
=> $m^3-5m+2=0$. $m=2$ will satisfy this equation
=> $\left(m-2\right)\left(m^2+2m-1\right)=0$. The other values of $m$ will not be a natural number.
=> $m=2$
Putting the value of m in $1$.
=> $2=\dfrac{\left(9+n^2\right)}{3n}$
=> $n^2-6n+9=0$
=> $n=3$
=> $a=nm=3*2=6$ and $b=nm^2=3*2^2=12$
=> $a+b+m+n=6+12+2+3=23$

questions.question_text: Find the largest positive integer $n$, so $n^3+100$ is perfectly divisible by $n+10$.
questions.solution_text:
Writing the given problem in terms of modulus, we have the equation, 
$n^3+100=\left(0\right)\left(mod\left(n+10\right)\right)$
Let a=n+10, we then have, n=a-10. 
Substituting this value for n in the above equation, we get, 
$\left(a-10\right)^3+100=a^3-1000-30a^2+300a+100$
$a^3-30a^2+300a-900=a\left(a^2-30a+300\right)-900$
Since, $a\left(a^2-30a+300\right)$ is clearly divisible by $a$, $a$ should also be a divisor of 900. 
The largest divisor of 900 is 900 itself.
And since we have $a=n+10$, the largest value a can take will be 900, and n can be at most 890. 
Hence, the largest positive integer value of n to satisfy the given conditions is 890.

questions.question_text: Three friends, A, B, and C, went to a restaurant. The amounts spent by A and C are in a 3:5 ratio. The ratio of the amount B spent to the total amount spent by A, B, and C is 2:5. Who spent the highest amount, and by what percentage was it greater than A’s spending?
questions.solution_text:
The ratio of the amount spent by B and all three friends = 2:5
Let us assume the proportionality constant as y. The amount spent by B = 2y and by all three friends = 5y
We are also told that the ratio of amounts spent by A and C is 3:5. 
Let us assume the proportionality constant as x. The amount spent by A will be 3x and by C will be 5x.
3x+2y+5x = 5y
8x = 3y
x = $\dfrac{3y}{8}$
The amount spent by C = $\dfrac{15y}{8}$
And the amount spent by A =  $\dfrac{9y}{8}$
The amount spent by B is more than the amount spent by C. So, B spent the highest amount.
$\dfrac{\left(2y-\frac{9y}{8}\right)}{\frac{9y}{8}}=\dfrac{\frac{7y}{8}}{\frac{9y}{8}}=\frac{7}{9} = 77.78$%

questions.question_text: A, B, and C together complete a job in 10 days. If they work in a cycle—A for 3 days, then B for 3 days, then C for 1 day—it takes 35 days to finish the same work. Now, if A and B work together for 11 days and then C joins at half efficiency, how many more days will it take to complete the work?
questions.solution_text:
A, B, and C together complete a job in 10 days. This means the total work done is -
$W=10A+10B+10C\rightarrow 1$
Now, they work in a cycle—A for 3 days, then B for 3 days, then C for 1 day. Now (3+3+1) = 7 days, and it takes 35 days to finish the same work, that is, they have done this for five cycles. This means total work is - 
$W=5\left(3A+3B+C\right)\rightarrow 2$
Since both the work done is the same, thus equating 1 and 2.
=> $10\left(A+B+C\right)=5\left(3A+3B+C\right)$
=> $C=A+B$
Thus, the total work done is $W=10A+10B+10C=10\left(C+C\right)=20C$
Now, A and B work together for 11 days. Thus, the work done is $11\left(A+B\right)=11C$. Now the remaining work is $9C$ and then C joins at half efficiency. Let the remaining number of days required be X.
=> $X\left(A+B+\dfrac{C}{2}\right)=9C$ and $A+B=C$
=> $X\left(\dfrac{3C}{2}\right)=9C$
=> $X=6 days$

questions.question_text: Ram bought an item with successive discounts of $x\%$ and $2x\%\ \left(x<25\right)$, and thus the overall price was $Y.$ If he had got two consecutive discounts of $2x\%$ and $4x\%$, then the overall cost would have been $\dfrac{Y}{4}$. Find the value of $2x$.
questions.solution_text:
Let us assume the value of the item to be 100. 
With successive discounts of $x\%$ and $\ 2x\%$, the overall price was $Y$.
=> $100\left(1-\dfrac{x}{100}\right)\left(1-\dfrac{2x}{100}\right)=Y\ \rightarrow①$
Now, with two consecutive discounts of $2x\%\ and\ 4x\%$, the overall cost is $Y/4$.
=> $100\left(1-\dfrac{2x}{100}\right)\left(1-\dfrac{4x}{100}\right)=\dfrac{Y}{4}\ \rightarrow②$
Assuming $\dfrac{x}{100}=a$ and then dividing ① by ②
=> $\dfrac{\left(1-a\right)\left(1-2a\right)}{\left(1-2a\right)\left(1-4a\right)}=4$
The term (1-2a) will be cancelled out, and thus - $\dfrac{1-a}{1-4a}=4$
=> $1-a=4-16a$
=> $15a=3$
=> $a=\dfrac{1}{5}$ => $x=20$
So, $2x=40$

BC = 8cm and CD = 6cm 
$\triangle BCD$ is a right-angled triangle. => $BD^2=BC^2+CD^2=6^2+8^2$
=> BD = 10cm
BE is the perpendicular bisector of AD. This means BE$\bot\ $AD and AE=DE.
In $\triangle ABE\ and\ \triangle DBE$- 
DE=AE, BE is the common side and $\angle BEA=\angle BED=90$, so by SAS congruency $\triangle ABE\ \simeq\ \triangle DBE$
=> AB=BD => AB = 10cm
Now, since CD = 6 cm, thus AF = 4cm
=> $AF^2+DF^2=AD^2$
=> $4^2+8^2=AD^2$ => $AD=4\sqrt{5}$
=> $AE=\dfrac{AD}{2}=2\sqrt{5}$
Now, $AE^2+BE^2=AB^2$
=> $\left(2\sqrt{5}\right)^2+BE^2=10^2$
=> $BE=4\sqrt{5}\ cm$

questions.question_text: When selling an article, the trader makes a profit of 20%. Had he sold it for Rs. 240 more, the profit percentage would have been 40%. If he gives two successive discounts of 5% and 10% on the marked price, he still earns a profit of 14%. Had he offered no discounts, what would be his profit percentage?
questions.solution_text:
Let the Cost price of the article be Rs. x
He makes a profit of 20%. $\therefore\ SP=\left(1+\dfrac{20}{100}\right)\times\ CP=1.2x$
If he sold it for Rs. 240 more, the SP $=1.2x\ +240$
And the profit percent becomes 40%
$\therefore\ \dfrac{\left(1.2x\ +240-x\right)}{x}=40\%=\dfrac{2}{5}$
$or,\ 5\times\ \left(0.2x\ +240\right)=2x$
$or,\ x=Rs.\ 1200$
Let the marked price be Rs. y
He offers 2 consecutive discounts of 5% and 10%. 
$\therefore\ \ SP=y\times\ \left(1-\dfrac{5}{100}\right)\times\ \left(1-\dfrac{10}{100}\right)=y.\ \dfrac{95}{100}.\ \dfrac{90}{100}$
In this case too he makes a profit of 14%. 
Hence, $\dfrac{\left(y.\ \dfrac{95}{100}.\ \dfrac{90}{100}\ -1200\right)}{1200}=14\%$
$or,\ y.\ \dfrac{95}{100}.\ \dfrac{90}{100}.\ \dfrac{1}{1200}-1=\dfrac{14}{100}$
$or,\ y.\ \dfrac{95}{100}.\ \dfrac{90}{100}.\ \dfrac{1}{1200}=\dfrac{114}{100}$
$or,\ y.\ =1600$
If he offered no discount then the SP would be the MP only , ie Rs. 1600
Then , $profit\ \%=\ \dfrac{\left(SP-CP\right)}{CP}\times\ 100=\dfrac{\left(1600-1200\right)}{1200}\times\ 100=\dfrac{400}{1200}\times\ 100=33.33\%$

questions.question_text: Kunal purchased 20 pens, each of a different colour. Find the number of arrangements possible for dividing these pens into four groups, each containing five pens.
questions.solution_text:
Initially, let there be 4 distinct groups named P, Q, R and S.
Now, the number of ways of selecting 5 pens for group P = $^{20}C_5$
Number of ways of selecting 5 pens for group Q from the remaining lot = $^{15}C_5$
Number of ways of selecting 5 pens for group R from the remaining lot = $^{10}C_5$ 
The remaining pens go to S
Total number of ways of selecting = $^{20}C_5$*$^{15}C_5$*$^{10}C_5$
Since the groups are identical, the number should be further divided by 4!
So, the required number of ways = $^{20}C_5$*$^{15}C_5$*$^{10}C_5$/4!
=> $\left[\dfrac{20!}{5!15!}\times\ \dfrac{15!}{5!10!}\times\ \dfrac{10!}{5!5!}\right]\times\ \dfrac{1}{4!}$
=> $\dfrac{20!}{4!\left(5!\right)^4}$
Option C is the correct answer.

Let the total amount invested be Rs. x. So, investment in Scheme A = Rs. 3x/5 and investment in Scheme B = Rs. 2x/5

$CI=\dfrac{3x}{5}\left[\left(1.1\right)^2-1\right]$
$CI=\dfrac{3x}{5}\left(1.21-1\right)$
$CI=\dfrac{3x}{5}\times\ 0.21=\dfrac{0.63x}{5}$
Interest from Scheme B (SI for 3 years at 12%):
$SI=\dfrac{P\times R\times T}{100}=\dfrac{2x}{5}\times12\times3\times\dfrac{1}{100}=\dfrac{72x}{500}=\dfrac{0.72x}{5}$
Total interest from A and B = Rs. 5,400
$\dfrac{0.63x}{5}+\dfrac{0.72x}{5}=\dfrac{1.35x}{5}=5400$
Upon solving, we get, $x=Rs,\ 20,000$
Now, we need to find the interest if Rs. 20,000 are invested for 2 years compounded semi-annually at the interest rate of 20%
Since the interest is compounded semi-annually, interest will be charged at the rate of 10% for each half year. 
$CI=P\left(1+\dfrac{r}{100}\right)^t-P$
$CI=20,000\left(1.1\right)^4-20,000$
$CI=20,000\left(1.4641\right)-20,000$
$CI=29,282-20,000=Rs.\ 9,282$
Hence, Rahul would receive 9282 - 5400 = Rs. 3,882 more interest.

questions.question_text: If $\log_a\left(4b+1\right)=2\ and\ \log_{2b}\left(a-1\right)=\dfrac{1}{2}$, then what will be the minimum value of $\left[\left(x+2a\right)^2+\left(x+b\right)^2\right]$

$\log_a\left(4b+1\right)=2$
=> $a^2=4b+1\ $ => $b=\frac{a^2-1}{4}\ \rightarrow\ ①$
and $\log_{2b}\left(a-1\right)=\dfrac{1}{2}$
=> $2b=\left(a-1\right)^2$ => $2b=a^2-2a+1$
Substituting the value of b from ①
=> $2\times\ \frac{a^2-1}{4}=a^2-2a+1$
=> $\ a^2-1=2a^2-4a+2$

But a cannot be 1, since the value of base in the logarithm can never be 1.
=> $a=3$, substituting this value in ①, we will get $b=2$
Now, we need to get the minimum value of $\left[\left(x+2a\right)^2+\left(x+b\right)^2\right]$
=> $f\left(x\right)=\left(x+6\right)^2+\left(x+2\right)^2$
=> $f\left(x\right)=2x^2+16x+40$
The above will have it's minimum value at $x=-\dfrac{b}{2a}=-\dfrac{16}{2\times\ 2}=-4$
Substituting the value of x in f(x)
=> $f\left(x\right)=2\left(-4\right)^2+16\left(-4\right)+40=8$
Thus, the minimum value is 8.

questions.question_text: If $\ A,B,C>0\ $ are three numbers such that $\ A+B+C=8\ $ then the maximum integral value of $AB+BC+CA$ is?
questions.solution_text:
Given, A, B, C are three positive numbers such that $A+B+C=8$
$\therefore\ \left(A+B+C\right)^2=8^2=64$______(1)
$or,\ A^2+B^2+C^2+2\left(AB+BC+CA\right)=64$  
Now, Using the $AM\ge GM\ $ inequality on $A^{2\ }\&\ B^2$ we get
$\dfrac{\left(A^{2\ }+\ B^2\right)}{2}\ge\sqrt{\ A^2B^2\ }=AB$
$or,\ A^2+B^2\ge2AB$
Similarly, $\ B^2+C^2\ge2BC$ and $\ C^2+A^2\ge2CA$
Adding these,
$\ 2\left(A^2+B^2+C^2\right)\ge2\left(AB+BC+CA\right)$
$\ or,\ A^2+B^2+C^2\ge AB+BC+CA$
Adding $2(AB+BC+CA)$ on both sides we get,
$\ A^2+B^2+C^2\ +2\left(AB+BC+CA\right)\ge3\left(AB+BC+CA\right)$
$\left(A+B+C\right)^2\ge3\left(AB+BC+CA\right)$
Now, by using eq. 1 - 
$\ 64\ge3\left(AB+BC+CA\right)$  
$\ or,\ \dfrac{64}{3}\ge\left(AB+BC+CA\right)$ .
So, $AB+BC+CA\le\frac{64}{3}=21.\overline{3}$
Hence, the maximum integral value of AB+BC+BC=21.

ALTERNATE SOLUTION 
We have A+B+C=8
Hence, AB+BC+CA will be maximum iff A=B=C=$\frac{8}{3}$
So, the maximum value of AB+BC+CA=$\frac{8}{3}\times\frac{8}{3}+\frac{8}{3}\times\frac{8}{3}+\frac{8}{3}\times\frac{8}{3}=\frac{64}{3}=21.333..$
And hence, the maximum integral value of AB+BC+CA is 21 .

questions.question_text: A railway line and a highway are laid parallel to each other. Car A, travelling at 72 km per hour, is overtaken by a train of length 300m in 20 seconds. 25 minutes later, the train has just completely overtaken another car, B, in 15 seconds. How much time after the train overtook car B will car A overtake car B? It is known that the three vehicles are travelling in the same direction.
questions.solution_text:
Let the speed of car A , car B and train be denoted by $v_A\ ,\ v_B,\ and\ v_T$ respectively.
Given , length of train is 300 m & $v_A\ =72kmph=72\times\ \ \dfrac{5}{18}=20\ mps$
The train crosses car A in 20 sec.
$\therefore\ \dfrac{L}{v_T-v_A}=20\ =>\ \dfrac{300}{v_T-20}=20\ $
$or,\ v_T=35\ mps$
Similarly, train crosses car B in 15 sec 
$\therefore\ \dfrac{300}{v_T-v_B}=15\ \ or,\ v_B=15\ mps$
Now we find the distance between car A and train 25 mins later. 
The distance between Car A and the back of the train is therefore $25\times\ 60\times\ v_T-25\times\ 60\times\ v_A$
$=25\times\ 60\times\left(\ v_T-v_A\right)=1500\times\ \left(35-20\right)=22500\ m$
This distance will have to be covered with a relative velocity of $\left(\ v_A-v_B\right)\ $ for car A to overtake car B.
Hence time taken $\ =\dfrac{22500}{\left(v_A-v_B\ \right)}=\dfrac{22500}{20-15}=\dfrac{22500}{5}=4500\ \sec$
So the time taken by car A to overtake car B is 4500 sec.
